label: Pyramid Texts
summary: The earliest surviving body of Egyptian religious writing, carved in late Dynasty 5 and Dynasty 6 royal pyramids. Whether the spells are funerary or reused temple ritual is debated in the archive.

relations.note: Precedence in surviving evidence, not replacement: Pyramid Text material continues to circulate.
Naydler reads the spells as records of living initiatory experience; mainstream scholarship treats them as mortuary ritual.

label: Coffin Texts
summary: Spells written on nonroyal coffins from the First Intermediate Period onward, concerned with bodily integrity, mobility, provisioning, and knowledge of the way.

label: The Amduat
aliases: book of what is in the underworld
summary: A New Kingdom royal composition mapping the twelve hours of the night as a route with named regions, beings, and gates.

relations.note: Both map the night, but they divide it differently and emphasise different judgments.

label: The Book of Gates
summary: A related underworld composition organised around guarded gates, with explicit sorting of the dead and of peoples.

label: Book of the Dead
aliases: book of going forth by day
summary: Individually commissioned spell collections with vignettes, used from the New Kingdom onward. No two copies are the same book.

label: The Teaching of Ptahhotep
summary: A wisdom text of maxims on listening, restraint, speech, hierarchy, and household conduct, framed as advice from an official to his successor.

relations.note: It presents maat as everyday conduct rather than as doctrine.

label: The Memphite Theology
summary: The account in which Ptah creates by conceiving in the heart and speaking with the tongue, transmitted on a stone that claims to copy a worm-eaten older document.

label: Plutarch, Isis and Osiris
summary: A Greek account written centuries after the pharaonic period. It supplies the most connected narrative of the Osiris myth and must be read as a late outside interpretation.

relations.note: Its continuous story is often read back into much earlier Egyptian material that never tells it that way.

label: Demotic and Greek magical papyri
summary: Late ritual handbooks combining Egyptian, Greek, and other traditions. They show operative ritual continuing under new languages and names.
